chunks: And he also narrated - from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Jamil from Zurarah ibn A'yan from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

There cannot be two Umras in one year. The meaning of these two narrations is that in the year, there is only one Umrah performed with the intention of Tamattu' (joining) to Hajj. As for the independent Umrah (not joined to Hajj), it is permissible in every month as we have previously stated. And whoever performs Umrah during the months of Hajj and then stays until the time of Hajj, it becomes a Tamattu' Umrah.

key_terms.مُتْعَةً: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are combined with a break)

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim perform Umrah more than once in a single year according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction in the reports by distinguishing between Umrat al-Tamattu' (which is unique to the Hajj season and limited to once a year) and Umrat al-Mufradah (which is independent and permissible in any month). He further clarifies that an independent Umrah performed during the Hajj months transforms into Umrat al-Tamattu' if the pilgrim remains in Mecca until the time of Hajj, a nuance critical for understanding the flexibility of Shia fiqh regarding pilgrimage rituals.
